title: हाम्रो निर्वाचन प्रणाली र सुधारका सम्भावनाहरू {Our electoral system and prospects for reform}
nepali: निर्वाचन प्रणाली लोकतन्त्रको आधार स्तम्भ हो l निर्वाचनको आवधिक अभ्यासमार्फत नागरिकले सार्वभौम अधिकारको प्रयोग गर्ने अवसर प्राप्त गर्छन्, संवैधानिक विकासले गतिशीलता प्राप्त गर्दछ र मुलुकको शासनले वैधानिकता प्राप्त गर्दछ । आवधिक निर्वाचनको अभ्यासबाट लोकतन्त्र जीवन्त हुन्छ । यस अर्थमा निर्वाचन लोकतन्त्रको प्राण वायु हो । विश्वमा विभिन्न प्रकृतिका निर्वाचन प्रणाली पाइन्छन् तापनि तिनले अङ्गीकार गरेका सारतत्व र आधारभूत मान्यता शाश्वत र विश्वव्यापी प्रकृतिका छन् l सम्बन्धित मुलुकको संवैधानिक संरचना, राजनैतिक शक्ति सन्तुलन र ऐतिहासिक परम्परा अनुसार विकसित हुने भए पनि आम रूपमा निर्वाचन प्रणालीहरू तीन प्रकारका पाइन्छन्  - पहिलो हुने निर्वाचित हुने प्रणाली, समानुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्वको प्रणाली तथा मिश्रित प्रणाली । नेपालमा अन्तरिम संविधानबमोजिम गठन भएको संविधान सभाको प्रयोजनका लागि तत्काल कायम रहेको द्वन्द्व व्यवस्थापन तथा  मुलुकका सबै जात, जाति, समुदायको प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित गर्न समानुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्वलाई बढी भार दिई समानुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व र पहिलो हुने निर्वाचित हुने समानान्तर मिश्रित निर्वाचन प्रणाली अपनाइएको थियो । त्यस यता, नेपालले अपनाएको निर्वाचन प्रणाली आफ्नै विशिष्टतासहितको मिश्रित छ । यो सैद्धान्तिक रूपमा सरल देखिन्छ l तर कानुनी, प्रक्रियागत, मत भार तथा क्लष्टर व्यवस्थापनको दृष्टिले अत्यन्त जटिल झन्झटिलो  छ । यो प्रणालीअन्तर्गत सबै तह र संरचनाको पहिलो निर्वाचन सम्पन्न भई स्थानीय तहको दोस्रो कार्यकालका लागि पनि निर्वाचन भइसकेको छ l  अन्य जनप्रतिनिधि संस्थाको निर्वाचन हुने अवस्था छ । यो अवधिमा निर्वाचन प्रणालीका सबल पक्ष र कमजोर पक्षको पहिचान भइसकेको छ l सुधार गर्नुपर्ने विषय स्पष्ट भएका छन् । यो सिकाइ र अनुभवको आधारमा निर्वाचन प्रणालीको नियमित सुधार गर्नु प्रत्येक लोकतान्त्रिक मुलुकको राष्ट्रिय एजेन्डा हुनु पर्दछ ।   Abstract in English   An electoral system is the foundation of democracy. Its periodic exercise enables citizens to realize their sovereign rights, enhances the legitimacy of governance and helps democracy to remain healthy from within. The design of a country’s electoral system depends on its constitutional arrangement, political power balance and historical tradition. It is also expected to embrace certain norms being practised universally. Among prominent electoral systems in the world are the first-past-the- post system, the proportional representation system and the mixed electoral system. Nepal has pursued the mixed electoral system, which in principle is simple and straight. However, it is very complex in terms of legal and procedural management. Following the completion of a round of elections to all levels and structures, the second round of local elections has also been completed. Preparations are on for the election to other representative bodies, including the Federal Parliament. In the process, electoral authorities have come across ample evidence of what works, what does not and where changes are needed. These lessons and experiences should drive the periodic reform of the electoral system in order to reinvigorate the democratic exercise.
american_english: An electoral system is the foundational pillar of democracy. Through the periodic practice of elections, citizens obtain the opportunity to exercise their sovereign rights, constitutional development gains dynamism, and the governance of the country gains legitimacy. Democracy becomes vibrant through the practice of periodic elections. In this sense, elections are the vital breath of democracy. Although electoral systems of varied nature are found in the world, the essence and fundamental principles adopted by them are of an enduring and universal character. Even though they evolve in accordance with the constitutional structure, political balance of power, and historical traditions of the country concerned, electoral systems are generally found in three types: the first-past-the-post system, the proportional representation system, and the mixed system. In Nepal, for the purpose of the Constituent Assembly formed under the Interim Constitution, a parallel mixed electoral system of proportional representation and first-past-the-post was adopted, according greater weight to proportional representation in order to manage the prevailing conflict and ensure the representation of all castes, ethnicities, and communities in the country. Since then, the electoral system adopted by Nepal has been a mixed one bearing its own distinctive characteristics. This appears simple in theory. However, from the standpoint of legal, procedural, vote-weight, and cluster management, it is extremely complex and cumbersome. Under this system, the first elections for all levels and structures have concluded, and elections for the second term of local bodies have also taken place. Elections for other representative institutions are poised to take place. During this period, the strengths and weaknesses of the electoral system have already been identified. The issues requiring reform have become clear. Periodic reform of the electoral system on the basis of these lessons and experiences must be a national agenda for every democratic country.

australian_english: An electoral system is the foundational pillar of democracy. Through the periodic practice of elections, citizens obtain the opportunity to exercise their sovereign rights, constitutional development gains momentum, and the governance of the nation gains legitimacy. Democracy remains vibrant through the exercise of periodic elections. In this sense, elections are the lifeblood of democracy. Although electoral systems of diverse character exist globally, the essence and foundational principles they embrace are enduring and universal in nature. Although they develop in line with the constitutional framework, political power balance and historical traditions of the respective country, electoral systems generally fall into three types: the first-past-the-post system, the proportional representation system, and the mixed system. In Nepal, for the purpose of the Constituent Assembly established under the Interim Constitution, a parallel mixed electoral system of proportional representation and first-past-the-post was adopted, according higher weight to proportional representation to manage ongoing conflict and secure representation for all castes, ethnicities and communities across the country. Ever since, the electoral system adopted by Nepal has been a mixed one, marked by its own distinctive features. This appears simple in theory. However, from the viewpoint of legal, procedural, vote-weight and cluster management, it is exceptionally complex and burdensome. Under this system, the inaugural elections across all tiers and structures have wrapped up, and elections for the second term of local government have likewise been held. Elections for other representative bodies are slated to take place. Over this period, the strengths and shortcomings of the electoral system have already been identified. The areas requiring reform have become evident. Regular reform of the electoral system on the basis of these learnings and experiences should form a national agenda for every democratic country.
informal_english: The electoral system is the cornerstone pillar of democracy itself. Through periodic elections only, citizens get the chance to exercise their sovereign rights, constitutional progress gains momentum, and the country's governance gets proper legitimacy. From the regular practice of elections, democracy stays fully vibrant and alive. In this sense, elections are the very life-breath of democracy. While different kinds of electoral systems are found across the world, the core essence and basic principles they adopt are eternal and universal only. Even if they develop according to the constitutional set-up, political balance of power, and historical traditions of each country, generally speaking, electoral systems are of three types: first-past-the-post, proportional representation, and the mixed system. In Nepal, for the Constituent Assembly constituted under the Interim Constitution, a parallel mixed system of proportional representation and first-past-the-post was adopted, giving extra weightage to proportional representation to tackle existing conflict and ensure representation for all castes, communities, and groups. Since that time, the electoral system adopted by Nepal has remained a mixed one with its own special peculiarities. On paper, this looks quite simple. But when it comes to legal aspects, procedures, vote-weightage, and cluster management, it is very complicated and cumbersome indeed. Under this system, the first round of elections for all tiers and setups got completed, and second-term elections for local levels have also taken place already. Elections for other representative bodies are also lined up to happen. Over this period, both the strong points and weak points of the electoral system have been clearly identified. The points needing reform have become completely clear. Based on this learning and experience, regular reform of the electoral system ought to be a top national agenda for every democratic country.
